promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 6 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Last week you ran 53 miles against a planned 38, and every session went past its distance, which is too big a jump to repeat. Next week brings the load back to 38 miles with one quality session, and the easy runs stay easy.

flags.title: Week overran the plan
flags.detail: 53 mi run against 38 planned, and every session went past its distance. Monday's rest day became a 4 mile run and a fourth threshold rep was added.

flags.title: Easy share fell
flags.detail: 54 percent of time in zones 1 and 2 against an 80 percent target. The extra miles and the fourth rep pushed too much time into harder zones.

flags.title: Calves and right knee
flags.detail: calves were tight Sunday night, and the right knee was sore in mid-August. Watch both this week, and see a professional if pain sharpens or keeps growing.

flags.title: Long-run effort
flags.detail: 20 miles at 3:20 with heart rate drifting up 7.4 bpm and most of the time in zone 3. The pace held, but the run was harder than an easy long run should be.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer:
Not at this volume. Feeling fine in the middle of a big week is common, but the cost of a jump like this often shows up a week or two later.

The 20 miles were a strong sign of endurance. The goal is to repeat that on a steadier build, not to stack more miles on top of it this week.

new.analysis:
## What the week showed
The week was not run as planned. Every session went past its distance, and the total landed about 15 miles over the plan. The longer runs and the extra rep are what changed the load, not one bad day.

| Measure | Planned | Ran |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weekly distance | 38 mi | 53 mi |
| Long run | 15 mi | 20 mi |
| Threshold reps | 3 | 4 |
| Easy share of time | 80% target | 54% |
| Relative effort | 223 (3-week average) | 423 |

## Why the load matters
A move from 37 to 53 miles is about 43 percent in one week. That is far beyond the gradual growth the build phase calls for. Tight calves on Sunday night are an early sign to respect, even though no pain was logged.

## What went right
The fitness signals are real. Easy pace dropped from 10:00 to 9:50 per mile at about the same heart rate of 139, and the back half of the 20 miler was not slower than the front half. The aerobic base is growing, which is the reason to keep building, just at a smaller step.

## Why next week looks as it does
Next week totals about 38 miles, which matches the planned total for the reviewed week. That gives the body a load it has already handled, while the extra volume settles. The quality session stays at one and is capped at three reps, because the fourth rep added hard time without a clear gain. Easy days are held under heart rate 145 so the easy share climbs back toward 80 percent. The long run drops to 14 miles so the legs recover from the 20, and marathon-pace work waits until the long run feels steady again.

## Longer view
Six weeks is enough time to rebuild, but only if the load grows in steps of about 10 percent. Once the calves feel normal and the easy runs stay easy, the weekly total should return to the mid-40s. The long run then climbs back to 18 to 20 miles, with marathon-pace segments added to some of them.
